title: Closed [e] — é, -er, -ez, -ed, et, les/des/mes (set 9)
sounds: les / des / mes / tes / ses / ces
focus: All of these make the closed [e]: lips spread, tongue high, a pure « ay » with no glide at the end. It's spelled é; -er, -ez and -ed at the end of a word (parler, chez, pied); the word « et »; and the short words les, des, mes, tes, ses, ces. Exceptions: in a few short words the -er is [ɛʁ] with the r pronounced (mer, fer, hiver, cher, hier), and « est » has the open [ɛ]. Québécois keeps é and è clearly apart, even at the end of a word (« parlé » vs « parlait »). « hiver » is one of the exceptions: its -er is [ɛʁ] with the r pronounced, so it isn't marked.

sentences.fr: En hiver, nous aimons all[er] dans l[es] Laurentides.
sentences.en: In winter, we like to go to the Laurentians.

sentences.fr: Nous faisons du ski [et] de la raquette.
Il fait très froid : il faut port[er] une tuque [et] d[es] mitaines.
sentences.en: It's very cold: you have to wear a toque and mittens.

sentences.fr: Le soir, nous jouons aux cartes [et] nous buvons du chocolat chaud.
sentences.en: In the evening, we play cards and drink hot chocolate.

sentences.fr: C'est mon moment pr[é]f[é]r[é] de l'ann[é]e !
sentences.en: It's my favourite time of the year!
